# Blueprint v0.3.5 — Deploy screen redesign + no duplicate servers

The Deploy step of the install-LLM wizard is reworked around its two
real phases, and auto-provision now guards against starting a second
server on top of one that's already running.

## Deploy is now a two-phase screen

Deploy used to render three tall status cards — runtime, weights,
server — the whole time, which pushed **Verify** (the part where you
actually talk to your model) far below the fold even after everything
was ready.

Now the screen matches what you're doing:

- **While setting up** — a single compact **checklist** walks itself
  through runtime → weights → server, one row each with a status icon,
  a one-line detail, and an inline progress bar while downloading. It
  runs automatically; any step that fails shows an inline **Retry**.
- **Once it's live** — the setup detail collapses to a slim
  **"your model is live"** strip (endpoint + pid, with a Details
  disclosure for the runtime/endpoint/weights/path, and a Stop button),
  and **Verify becomes the focus** right below it — no scrolling to
  send a test prompt. The server log tucks into a collapsed drawer at
  the bottom, and **Continue to Dashboard** finishes the flow.

## Auto-provision no longer double-starts the server

Before starting llama-server, Deploy now probes the local
`/health` endpoint. If a server is already answering on the port, it
reconciles to that one instead of spawning a second process — which
previously could happen when the supervisor briefly reported "stopped"
while a server was in fact still up, leaving two llama-servers fighting
for port 8080. The result: a cleaner start, and no stray duplicate
processes.

## Other platforms

Both changes live in the shared frontend, so macOS and Linux get them
too.
